title: Inside UVA's Research on Reincarnation, Near-Death Experiences, and more
excerpt: Discover the fascinating findings of UVA perceptual studies, challenging conventional views on consciousness and near-death experiences.
content:
For almost 60 years, the University of Virginia School of Medicine’s Division of Perceptual Studies (DOPS) has contested conventional scientific thought regarding human consciousness, capacity, and remarkable experiences. While studying phenomena such as near-death experiences and altered states of consciousness, DOPS has gathered evidence supporting the idea that the human mind operates independently from the brain and that human consciousness survives after death.

These are not your average ghost stories—in fact, they’re not ghost stories at all. Rather, DOPS seeks to explain the unexplainable. Last year Dr. Phillip Cozzolico, an associate professor of research at DOPS, and his team published Past-life Memories and Foreign Languages, a study of children who can inexplicably speak foreign languages without formal instruction. This is part of DOPS’ greater research on “cases of the reincarnation type” (CORT), which includes kids with unexplained memories of a previous life.

Dr. David J. Acunzo, assistant professor at DOPS, researches “psi”—psychic phenomena such as telepathy, precognition, and clairvoyance using state-of-the-art technology. And there’s also, Dr. Bruce Greyson, former director of DOPS, who has researched over 1,000 cases of near-death experiences in his 50 years at UVA. 

These scientists are conducting scientific research, not speculation. Though a bit goosebump-inducing, DOPS’ academics pose thought-provoking questions that beckon further research into the supernatural—an unusual endeavor for some, but everyday work for them. Med.Virginia.edu

This article originally appeared in the October 2026 issue.
